brief: Python interface module to Zymkey Application Utilities Library.
intro:
This file contains a Python class which interfaces to the the Zymkey
Application Utilities library. Systems intending to run such applications
require that the `python3-zku` package be installed.

This class facilitates writing userspace applications which use Zymkey to
perform cryptographic operations, such as:

1. Signing of payloads using ECDSA
2. Verification of payloads that were signed using Zymkey
3. Exporting the public key that matches Zymkey's private key
4. "Locking" and "unlocking" data objects
5. Generating random data

Additionally, there are methods for changing the i2c address (i2c units
only), setting tap sensitivity, and controlling the LED.

items.name: lock
items.signature: def lock(src: t.Union[str, bytes], dst: t.Optional[str] = None, encryption_key: str = ZYMKEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY) -> t.Union[None, bytearray]
items.brief: Lock up source (plaintext) data.
items.details:
This methods encrypts and signs a block of data.

The Zymkey that can be used for locking/unlocking operations

1. The one-way key is meant to lock up data only on the local host
   computer. Data encrypted using this key cannot be exported and
   deciphered anywhere else.

params.name: src
params.description:
The source (plaintext) data to lock.

If a `str` is passed to this method, the value is assumed to be
the absolute path to the location of the source file. If `bytes`
or `bytesarray` is passed, it is assumed to contain binary data.

params.name: dst
params.description:
The destination (ciphertext) of the locked data.

If a `str` is passed to this method, the value is assumed to be
the absolute path to the location of the file where the destination
data is meant to be written. Otherwise, if `None` is passed to the
method (the default), the locked data is returned from the method
as a bytearray.

params.name: encryption_key
params.description:
This specifies which key will be used to lock the data. A value of
'zymbit' (default) specifies that the Zymkey will use the one-way
key.

returns.description:
The locked data is returned as a bytearray if no destination is
specified when this method is called. Otherwise, `None` is returned.

throws.description: If `ret` is a bad return code from the Zymkey library function.

items.name: unlock
items.signature: def unlock(src: t.Union[str, bytes], dst: t.Optional[str] = None, encryption_key: str = ZYMKEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, raise_exception: bool = True) -> t.Union[None, bytearray, t.NoReturn]
items.brief: Unlock source (ciphertext) data.
items.details:
This method verifies a locked object signature and decrypts the
associated ciphertext data.

The Zymkey has two keys that can be used for locking/unlocking operations

1. The one-way key is meant to lock up data only on the local host
   computer. Data encrypted using this key cannot be exported and
   deciphered anywhere else.

params.name: src
params.description:
The source (ciphertext) data to verify and decrypt.

If a `str` is passed to this method, the value is assumed to be
the absolute path to the location of the source file. If `bytes`
or `bytesarray` is passed, it is assumed to contain binary data.

params.name: dst
params.description:
The destination of the decrypted data (plaintext).

If a `str` is passed to this method, the value is assumed to be
the absolute path to the location of the file where the destination
data is meant to be written. Otherwise, if `None` is passed to the
method (the default), the locked data is returned from the method
as a bytearray.

params.name: encryption_key
params.description:
This specifies which key will be used to lock the data. A value of
'zymbit' (default) specifies that the Zymkey will use the one-way
key.

params.name: raise_exception
params.description:
Specifies if an exception should be raised if the signature verification
of the locked object fails.

returns.description:
The locked data is returned as a bytearray if no destination is
specified when this method is called. Otherwise, `None` is returned.

throws.description: If `ret` is a bad return code from the Zymkey library function.

items.name: sign
items.signature: def sign(src: t.Union[str, bytes, bytearray], slot: int = 0, return_recid: bool = False, encoding: str = 'utf-8', digest: t.Any = None) -> bytearray
items.brief: Generate a signature using the Zymkey's ECDSA private key.

params.name: src
params.description: The SHA256 digest of the data that will be used to generate the signature.

params.name: slot
params.description: The key slot used for signing. \[ZYMKEY5, HSM60, HSM64, HSM6\] Slot can't contain a X25519 key pair

params.name: return_recid
params.description: This parameter asks for the y parity to be returned.

params.name: encoding
params.description: This parameter asks for the encoding for the string source.

params.name: digest
params.description: This parameter asks for the type of hash. Can be None. Defaults to sha256.

returns.description: A bytearray of the signature.
If return_recid = True, then return the y parity of the signature (either a 1 or 0).

notes.text: Allow for overloading of source parameter in similar fashion to lock/unlock.

items.name: sign_digest
items.signature: def sign_digest(digest: t.Any, slot: int = 0, return_recid: bool = False) -> bytearray
items.brief: Generate a signature using the Zymkey's ECDSA private key.

params.name: digest
params.description: A encoded str instance representing the digest to be signed.

params.name: slot
params.description: This parameter specifies the key slot used for signing. \[ZYMKEY5, HSM60, HSM64, HSM6\] Slot can't contain a X25519 key pair

params.name: return_recid
params.description: This parameter asks for the y parity to be returned.

returns.description: The signature of the SHA-256 digest passed to this method.
If return_recid = True, then return the y parity of the signature (either a 1 or 0).

throws.description: If `ret` is a bad return code from the Zymkey library function.

notes.text: Allow for overloading of source parameter in similar fashion to lock/unlockData.

items.name: verify
items.signature: def verify(src: t.Union[str, bytes, bytearray], sig: bytearray, raise_exception: bool = True, pubkey_slot: int = 0, foreign: bool = False, encoding: str = 'utf-8', digest: t.Any = None) -> bool
items.brief: Verify data against a signature.
items.details:
The public key is not specified in the parameter list to ensure
that the public key that matches the Zymkey's ECDSA private key
is used.

params.name: src
params.description: The buffer to verify.

params.name: sig
params.description: The signature to verify against.

params.name: raise_exception
params.description:
By default, when verification fails a `VerificationError` will be
raised, unless this is set to `False`.

params.name: pubkey_slot
params.description:
The key slot to use to verify the signature against. Defaults to the
first key slot.

params.name: foreign
params.description:
If false, the normal key store is referenced. Otherwise, the foreign
public key store is referenced.
**Note:** This parameter is only applicable for Supported Devices: ZYMKEY5, HSM60, HSM64, HSM6, Secure Compute Module.

params.name: encoding
params.description: This parameter asks for the encoding for the string source.

params.name: digest
params.description: This parameter asks for the type of hash. Can be None. Defaults to sha256.

returns.description:
Returns `True` for a good verification or `False` for a bad
verification when the `raise_exception` parameters is `False`.

items.name: verify_digest
items.signature: def verify_digest(digest: t.Any, sig: bytearray, raise_exception: bool = True, pubkey_slot: int = 0, foreign: bool = False) -> bool
items.brief: Verify a signature using the Zymkey's ECDSA public key.
items.details:
The public key is not specified in the parameter list to ensure
that the public key that matches the Zymkey's ECDSA private key
is used.

params.name: digest
params.description: A hashlib instance that will be used to generate the signature.

params.name: sig
params.description: The signature to verify.

params.name: raise_exception
params.description:
By default, when verification fails, a `VerificationError` will be
raised, unless this is set to `False`.

params.name: pubkey_slot
params.description:
The key slot to use to verify the signature against. Defaults to
the first key slot.

params.name: foreign
params.description:
If false, the normal key store is referenced. Otherwise, the foreign
public key store is referenced.
**Note:** This parameter is only applicable for Supported Devices: ZYMKEY5, HSM60, HSM64, HSM6, Secure Compute Module.

returns.description:
Returns `True` for a good verification or `False` for a bad
verification when `raise_exception` is `False`.

items.name: ecdh
items.signature: def ecdh(local_slot: int, peer_pubkey: t.Union[t.List[bytes], int], kdf_func_type: str = 'none', salt: t.Optional[t.List[bytes]] = [], info: t.Optional[t.List[bytes]] = [], num_iterations: int = 1, peer_pubkey_slot_is_foreign: bool = True, derived_key_size: bool = 32) -> bytearray
items.brief: Derive a key or a pre-master secret from an ECDH operation.

params.name: local_slot
params.description: The local key slot to use.

params.name: peer_pubkey
params.description:
The public key of the peer used to generate the pre-master secret
against the private key located in `local_slot`. This parameter can
be a list of `bytes` if the key is provided explicitly or an `int`
if it refers to a key slot.

params.name: kdf_func_type
params.description:
Specifies the KDF (Key Derivation Function) to use
for the returned derived key. Valid values are:

* `"none"`: just return the pre-master secret. NOTE: The raw pre-master
  secret should not be used as a derived key should be put through a
  suitable KDF. Use 'none' when it is desired to use a different KDF
  than what is offered by this method.
* `"rfc5869-sha256"`: RFC5869 with SHA256
* `"rfc5869-sha512"`: RFC5869 with SHA512
* `"pbkdf2-sha256"`: PBKDF2 with SHA256
* `"pbkdf2-sha512"`: PBKDF2 with SHA512

params.name: salt
params.description: A unique identifier for KDF. Ignored for `kdf_func_type='none'`.

params.name: info
params.description: A unique field for rfc5869. Ignore for other KDF types.

params.name: num_iterations
params.description: The number of iterations that the KDF should complete.

params.name: peer_pubkey_slot_is_foreign
params.description: TODO_DESCRIPTION

params.name: derived_key_size
params.description: TODO_DESCRIPTION

returns.description: The computed signature.

notes.text: Allow for overloading of source parameter in similar fashion to lock/unlockData.

items.details: This method stores a foreign public key onto the Zymkey foreign public keyring.

params.name: pubkey

items.name: disable_public_key_export
items.brief: Disable exporting of a public key at a given slot.
items.details:
This method permanently disables exporting a public key from a
given slot.

params.name: slot
params.description: This parameter specifies the key slot for the public key.

params.name: foreign
params.description: If true, the slot refers to the foreign public keyring.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: gen_key_pair
items.brief: Generate a new key pair.
items.details: This method generates a new key pair of the specified type.

params.name: key_type
params.description:
This parameter indicates the EC curve type that should be
associated with the new key pair.

returns.description: the slot allocated to the key or less than one for failure.

items.name: gen_ephemeral_key_pair
items.brief: Generate a new ephemeral key pair.
items.details:
This method generates a new ephemeral key pair of the specified
type, overwriting the previous ephemeral key pair.

params.name: key_type
params.description:
This parameter indicates the EC curve type that should be
associated with the new key pair.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: remove_key
items.brief: Remove a key at the designated slot.
items.details:
This method removes a key at the designated slot in either the
standard key store or the foreign public keyring.

params.name: slot
params.description: This parameter specifies the key slot for the key.

params.name: foreign
params.description: If true, a public key in the foreign keyring will be deleted.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: invalidate_ephemeral_key
items.brief: Invalidate the ephemeral key.
items.details:
This method invalidates the ephemeral key, effectively removing
it from service until a new key is generated.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

throws.description: If `ret` is a bad return code from the Zymkey library function.

items.name: gen_wallet_master_seed
items.brief: Generates a new master seed for creating a new BIP32 wallet.
items.details:
This method generates a new master seed for creating a new BIP32
wallet.

params.name: key_type
params.description:
This parameter indicates the EC curve type that should be
associated with the new key pair.

params.name: master_gen_key
params.description:
The master generator key (bytearray) used in the
derivation of the child key.

params.name: wallet_name
params.description:
The name of the wallet (string) that this master seed
is attached to.

params.name: recovery_strategy
params.description:
RecoveryStrategy() class that defines what strategy to be used
{None, BIP39, SLIP39} are currently supported.
RecoveryStrategy->passphrase must be b64 encoded.

returns.description: the slot the master seed was generated in. 0 for starting SLIP39 sessions.

items.name: set_gen_SLIP39_group_info
items.brief: Configures the number of members and threshold for the group shares.
items.details:
This method sets the number of members required for a group share once a SLIP39 session
was opened via gen_wallet_master_seed().

params.name: group_index
params.description:
This parameter indicates the index of the group share
to set the amount of member count/threshold for.

params.name: member_count
params.description: The total number of members (mnemonics) in this group share.

params.name: member_threshold
params.description: The number of members (mnemonics) needed to reconstruct the group share.

returns.description: 0 on successful configuration. non-zero for error.

items.name: add_gen_SLIP39_member_pwd
items.brief: Generates a new mnemonic_str tied to a SLIP39 member.
items.details:
This method generates a new member of a group share. Members can also be
passphrase protected. Passphrases are not required to be unique. This
function is meant to be called after configuring a group via set_gen_SLIP39_group_info().

params.name: passphrase
params.description:
This parameter indicates the passphrase of the SLIP39 member
and is associated with the mnemonic string generated. Can
be empty string for no passphrase.

returns.description: A 24-word recovery phrase known as a mnemonic sentence. non-zero for error.

items.name: cancel_SLIP39_session
items.brief: Cancels an active SLIP39 session.
items.details: This method cancels an ongoing SLIP39 session for both master seed generation and recovery.

returns.description: 0 on success. non-zero for error.

items.name: gen_oversight_wallet
items.signature: def gen_oversight_wallet(key_type, pub_key, chain_code, node_addr, wallet_name, variant='')
items.brief: Generates a supervisory bip32 wallet.
items.details:
This method generates a new supervisory Bip32 wallet. Meant for
read-only transactions and supervising history.

params.name: key_type
params.description:
This parameter indicates the EC curve type that should be
associated with the new key pair.

params.name: pub_key
params.description:
The public key (bytearray) of the last
hardened node of the node address.

params.name: chain_code
params.description:
The chain code (bytearray) of the last
hardened node of the node address.

params.name: node_addr
params.description: The bip32 node address used. (EX: "m/1852'/1815'/0'").

params.name: wallet_name
params.description:
The name of the wallet (string) that this master seed
is attached to.

params.name: variant
params.description:
Key type variant to generate from. Currently only "cardano" is
supported for "ed25519".

returns.description: the slot the oversight wallet was generated in.

items.name: gen_wallet_child_key
items.brief: Generates a child key based on a parent key that is in a wallet.
items.details:
This method generates a child key based on a parent key that is
in a wallet.

params.name: parent_key_slot
params.description:
This parameter specifies the parent key slot. This
key must already be part of a wallet.

params.name: index
params.description:
This parameter represents the index for the child key
derivation which becomes part of the node address.

params.name: hardened
params.description: If true, the key is a hardened key.

params.name: return_chain_code
params.description:
If true, returns the chain code for the key as well.
(Must be from a hardened key).

returns.description: the allocated slot on success, or a tuple containing the chain code as well.

items.name: restore_wallet_master_seed
items.signature: def restore_wallet_master_seed(key_type, master_gen_key, wallet_name, recovery_strategy, mnemonics=None)
items.brief: Restore a wallet's master seed based on the recovery strategy object.
items.details:
This method restores a wallet's master seed based on a
mnemonic string and a master generator key. This method can be
used in the process of wallet duplication.

params.name: key_type
params.description:
This parameter indicates the EC curve type that should be
associated with the new key pair.

params.name: master_gen_key
params.description:
The master generator key used in the derivation of
the child key.

params.name: wallet_name
params.description: Name of the new wallet to be generated.

params.name: recovery_strategy
params.description:
RecoveryStategy class object that provides the type of recovery
and key variant required for restoration.

params.name: mnemonics
params.description:
Mnemonic sentences required for restoration, number of mnemonics dependant
on recovery strategy used. This field is not used for SLIP39.

returns.description: the allocated slot on success

items.name: add_restore_SLIP39_mnemonic
items.brief: Feed a mnemonic string and the passphrase associated with it.
items.details:
This method feeds in mnemonic sentences (shards) into the module.
Meant to be called after starting a restore_wallet_master_seed() SLIP39 session.
Will return -1 until the master seed is reconstructed properly.

params.name: mnemonic_sentence
params.description: 24-word recovery phrase associated with the SLIP39 member.

params.name: passphrase
params.description:
This parameter indicates the passphrase of the SLIP39 member
and is associated with the mnemonic string generated. Can
be empty string for no passphrase.

returns.description:
A -1 for no change in status. Otherwise returns the slot of the master seed successfully
reconstructed from the last shard passed in.

items.name: get_wallet_node_addr
items.brief: Get a wallet node address from a key slot
items.details:
This method gets a wallet entry's node address from its key slot
assignment. The wallet name and master seed slot are also
returned.

params.name: slot
params.description: The key slot assignment.

returns.description: the node address, wallet name and master seed key slot.

items.name: get_wallet_key_slot
items.brief: Look up a wallet key slot number from a node address
items.details:
This method gets a wallet key slot number from its node address
and wallet name or master seed key slot. Either the wallet name
or the master seed slot must be present.

params.name: node_addr
params.description: The desired node address to look up

params.name: wallet_name
params.description:
The name of the wallet that the node address belongs
to. Either this parameter or master_seed_slot must be
specified or this function will fail.

params.name: master_seed_slot
params.description:
The master seed slot that the node address belongs
to. Either this parameter or wallet_name must be
specified or this function will fail.

returns.description: the key slot.

items.name: set_i2c_address
items.brief: Set the i2c address of the Zymkey.
items.details:
**Note:** This is only applicable to versions of the Zymkey with i2c.

This method should be called if the i2c address of the
Zymkey is shared with another i2c device on the same i2c bus.
The default i2c address for Zymkey units is 0x30. Currently,
the address may be set in the ranges of 0x30 - 0x37 and 0x60 - 0x67.

After successful completion of this command, the Zymkey will
reboot itself.

params.name: address
params.description: The i2c address that the Zymkey will set itself to.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

throws.description: If `ret` is a bad return code from the Zymkey library function.

items.name: set_tap_sensitivity
items.brief: Set the sensitivity of tap operations.
items.details:
This method permits setting the sensitivity of the tap
detection feature. Each axis may be individually
configured or all at once.

params.name: axis
params.description:
The axis to configure. Valid values include:
  1. 'all': Configure all axes with the specified sensitivity value.
  2. 'x' or 'X': Configure only the x-axis
  3. 'y' or 'Y': Configure only the y-axis
  4. 'z' or 'Z': Configure only the z-axis

params.name: pct
params.description:
The sensitivity expressed as percentage.
  1. 0% = Shut down: Tap detection should not occur along the axis.
  2. 100% = Maximum sensitivity.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: wait_for_tap
items.brief: Wait for tap event
items.details:
This function is called in order to wait for a tap event to occur.
This function blocks the calling thread unless called with a
timeout of zero.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description:
The maximum amount of time in milliseconds to wait for a tap
event to arrive.

items.name: get_accelerometer_data
items.brief: Get current accelerometer data and tap info.
items.details:
This function gets the most recent accelerometer data in units of g
forces plus the tap direction per axis.

returns.type: An array of accelerometer readings in units of g-force.
returns.description:
array index 0 = x axis
            1 = y axis
            2 = z axis
A value of -1 indicates that the tap event was detected in a
negative direction for the axis, +1 for a positive direction
and 0 for stationary.

items.name: get_time
items.brief: Get current GMT time
items.details:
This function is called to get the time directly from a
Zymkey's Real Time Clock (RTC)

params.name: precise
params.description:
If true, this API returns the time after the next second
falls. This means that the caller could be blocked up to one second.
If False, the API returns immediately with the current time reading.

items.name: set_perimeter_event_actions
items.brief: Set perimeter breach action
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when a perimeter breach
event occurs. The possible actions are any combination of:
  * Notify host
  * Zymkey self-destruct

params.name: channel
params.description: The channel (0 or 1) that the action flags will be applied to

params.name: action_notify
params.description: Set a perimeter breach to notify. (default = True)

params.name: action_self_destruct
params.description: Set a perimeter breach to self destruct. (default = False)

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.details:
This function is called in order to wait for a perimeter breach
event to occur. This function blocks the calling thread unless
called with a timeout of zero.

params.name: timeout_ms

(input) The maximum amount of time in milliseconds to wait for a perimeter breach
event to arrive.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_battery_voltage_action
items.brief: Set battery voltage action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the
battery voltage falls below the threshold set by
set_battery_voltage_threshold. If this function is never
called, do nothing is default. There are three actions:
  * Do nothing
  * Go to sleep until battery is replaced
  * Self-destruct
With sleep and self_destruct set to False, it removes a
previously set sleep or self_destruct action.

params.name: sleep
params.description: Set the sleep action.

params.name: self_destruct
params.description: Set the self_destruct action.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_battery_voltage_threshold
items.brief: Sets the battery voltage threshold.
items.details:
This function sets the threshold at which if the
battery voltage falls bellow, the action set by
set_battery_voltage_action will be carried out.
The recommended threshold is 2.3V is assumed by default. Threshold
must be below 2.5V.

params.name: threshold
params.description: The threshold in Volts.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_cpu_temp_action
items.brief: Set HSM CPU temperature threshold action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the
HSM CPU temperature falls below the threshold set by
set_cpu_low_temp_threshold, or rises above the threshold
set by set_cpu_high_temp_threshold. There are two
actions to apply:
  * Do nothing
  * Self-destruct
To remove a previously set self-destruct action, call
this function with self_destruct=False.

params.name: self_destruct
params.description: Set the self_destruct action.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_cpu_low_temp_threshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU low temperature threshold.
items.details:
This function sets the threshold at which if the
on-board HSM CPU's tempreature falls below, the
action set by set_cpu_temp_action will be carried out.
WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if
you set a threshold above the CPU's ambient temperature.
The recommended setting is no more than 20C.
If this function is never called, -10 degrees celsius is
assumed.

params.name: threshold
params.description: The threshold in celsius.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_cpu_high_temp_threshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU high temperature threshold.
items.details:
This function sets the threshold at which if the
on-board HSM CPU's tempreature rises above, the
action set by set_cpu_temp_action will be carried out.
WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if
you set a threshold below the CPU's ambient temperature.
The recommended setting is no less than 40C.
If this function is never called, 65 degrees celsius is
assumed.

params.name: threshold
params.description: The threshold in celsius.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: set_supervised_boot_policy

- 1 Self-Destruct
- 2 Hold Chip in Reset

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: remove_supervised_boot_file

items.details:

be checked by Supervised boot during the boot process.

params.name: filepath
params.description: The file to be removed from the manifest.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: get_supervised_boot_file_manifest
items.brief: Get the file manifest for Supervised boot to check.
items.details:
This function gets a list of the files that are checked
by Supervised boot during the boot process.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.
File manifest to be checked by Supervised boot.
